method: All four controls run through the REAL benchmark_runner path - a genuine harbor run -a oracle --n-attempts 1 against the live gym for each variant, not a local re-score. Each control edited solution/artifact_plan.json (the exact file write_artifacts.py stages into /workspace), ran a real oracle job under a new --job-name, and was reverted to the byte-identical original (diff-confirmed) before the next control. A final oracle re-run (job email8b-oracle-final-v2) after the last revert confirmed reward 1.0 on the clean bundle again, and evaluations/oracle/ is built from the separate email8b-oracle-fix1 run (the same unmodified artifact_plan.json, run immediately before this battery to confirm the corrected 1-week-window design).

notes: Strictness measured over the two semantic-shaped mutants actually run (one corrupted numeric field, one corrupted named-string field) - 2 of 2 caught cleanly with no collateral failures on either run. The 5 database_state write-back checks and the 3 rubric_checks were not separately semantic-mutated in this battery via artifact_plan.json, because artifact_plan.json only controls the JSON deliverable's content, not the live gym's database state or the agent's trace - their real behavior was instead independently exercised by: (a) the write-back checks' own positive proof, since the seed carries no draft addressed to Morgan Thompson at all (a run that never wrote back, or wrote to the wrong person/meeting, would score 0 on these regardless of the JSON file's content); and (b) the rubric_checks, validated separately against constructed adversarial and technically-correct-but-unreasoned trace/reply cases using the REAL production grading path (see rubric_validation_summary below), the appropriate validation method for a trace- or final-answer-graded check per connector-task-miner.md's guidance.

rubric_validation_summary.note: This task's three rubric checks (real_meeting_classified_by_structural_fields and decline_vs_tentative_correctly_distinguished, both target: trace; final_reply_states_a_genuine_conclusion, target: final_answer) were validated by calling the REAL, PRODUCTION grading path directly - tests/test_outputs.py's _model_response_from_evidence and _execute_rubric_check_verifier (which wraps verifier_engine.py's VerifierEngine._execute_rubric_check_verifier, the exact same code the live oracle/agent grading run executes), imported and invoked with a constructed evidence dict, calling the real GLM judge endpoint (http://34.41.10.8:4000/v1/chat/completions, model glm-5.2, temperature 0, via litellm) for real. This supersedes an earlier round's validation script, which fed the judge a hand-rolled prompt and a fabricated observation_note trace field that _build_trace_evidence never actually produces (a real harbor_check finding: layer5_verifier_fairness_static__counterfactual_strength) - the corrected script constructs trace evidence in the EXACT shape _build_trace_evidence emits (a JSON list of {name, args, result} tool-call entries) plus the real agent_messages narration field (also newly wired into the production trace-target path by this round's fix to verifier_engine.py/test_outputs.py, see task.toml/consistency/shortcut_audit.md and the layer5_llm_judge_design__judge_context_completeness fix). Nine constructed cases were tested (three per rubric: gold, adversarial-wrong, and technically-correct-but-unreasoned), plus two repeat runs of the gold case at temperature 0 to confirm stability, all against a genuinely live judge call. Raw results: consistency/rubric_validation_raw.json (shipped alongside this file) - the summary below quotes every verdict and motivation verbatim from that file.

rubric_validation_summary.mismatch_found_and_disposition: Even against the corrected, real-production-path evidence shape, 10 of 11 constructed cases (including both stability repeats) matched expectation exactly. The one mismatch (decline_vs_tentative_correctly_distinguished's technically-correct-but-unreasoned case) reproduces identically to an earlier round's finding under the OLD (fabricated observation_note) evidence shape, which confirms it is a genuine property of the rubric's own PASS criterion, not an artifact of the counterfactual_strength bug that round's validation script had. On inspection, this rubric's PASS criterion ('any route to that outcome passes equally: reading fields off the bulk search response, or any per-entry follow-up' - the same 'any route passes equally' principle used identically in real_meeting_classified_by_structural_fields) treats a correct WRITE-BACK TARGET itself (drafting specifically about Technical Interview, addressed only to Morgan Thompson, with zero correspondence touching Skip Level 1:1) as sufficient behavioral evidence that decline was distinguished from tentative - a wrong method could not have produced that exact targeting by chance, since chasing the wrong meeting or drafting to nobody would have been the naive failure mode. This is not a discrimination gap unique to the constructed test case: the REAL oracle's own trace (emit_oracle_trajectory.py's output) contains no narrated reasoning prose at all - only raw tool-call names and arguments - and yet the real live GLM judge legitimately scored this exact rubric PASS against that real, narration-free trace in email8b-oracle-fix1 and email8b-oracle-final-v2. Tightening the rubric to require explicit narrated reasoning would make the task's own legitimate gold reference fail its own rubric, which would be a self-inflicted bug, not a fix. Disposition: no change made to this rubric. The mismatch is recorded here as a genuine, honestly-reported finding rather than silently omitted.
rubric_validation_summary.consistency_at_temperature_0: Confirmed by two independent repeat calls of the gold case for both trace rubrics (rubric1_gold_repeat2, rubric2_gold_repeat2) - both returned the identical PASS verdict at temperature 0, and additionally by the real oracle run itself: the live rubric_check fired for real during email8b-oracle-fix1 and email8b-oracle-final-v2 and returned PASS both times against the same real (non-constructed) golden trajectory trace.
